openObligations: The admitted primary acquisition is8.3 mM bovine pancreatic trypsin inhibitor at pH*5.2 in isotope-enriched aqueous emulsion droplets at-10 and-30 C. pH* is uncorrected for isotope effects. This is not a physiological-temperature cellular solution or an ionic-shell experiment.

The measured quantities are longitudinal relaxation recovery/dispersion of 2H and 17O water nuclei relative to same-isotope bulk-water references. Hydration water is not separately resolved as an independent resonance because of exchange.

Lorentzian amplitudes/correlation times, water-class assignments and rotational retardation are source-model inferences. The fixed hydration number268 is estimated from existing5PTI solvent-accessible area,1.4 angstrom probe and 15 square-angstrom area per water; it is not a direct counted population.

The reported beta amplitudes are apparent Nbeta*Sbeta^2 products affected by exchange and orientational order. They are not integer water counts, unique hydration-site occupancies or directly measured residence times.

The highest-frequency point is excluded from the source mono-Lorentzian fits. A weak second component is suggested; its amplitude and the frequency-independent term have large covariance. Missing raw data and full covariance prevent an independent fit or unique distribution reconstruction.

Protein rotational times14/70 ns at-10/-30 C are viscosity/isotope/hydrodynamic-scaled adopted estimates from earlier relaxation, not new direct measurements of tumbling in these samples. Surface/internal separation depends on these and exchange assumptions.

SI S7 notes that the expected W111 internal-water behavior at-30 C is inconsistent with the observed dispersion. A local structural transformation causing much slower exchange is proposed but not measured; complete external-surface attribution remains conditional.

The source infers modest mobility retardation for most surface-contact waters, not static long-range ordering, an immobilized shell, a universal no-more-than-two bound at all temperatures, or the same timescale at every residue.

Converting rotational relaxation into residence/translational times requires additional assumptions. The source24 ps estimate at 4 C and room-temperature extrapolations are not direct primary observations at those temperatures and are not admitted as new measurements.

No ion positions, ion number/density, electrostatic potential, hydrogen-bond energy, dielectric shell, catalysis, recognition change, binding thermodynamics or protein-stability perturbation is measured by the selected acquisition.

Long-range dipolar contributions to an NOE measurement describe nonlocal magnetic sampling. They do not establish long-range structural ordering of water or ions. The paper new oxytocin and older BPTI NOE analyses are read but supply no additional admitted acquisition context or independent replication here.

The emulsion-interface control, BPTI self-association estimates, internal-water coordinates and stability/cold-denaturation arguments include earlier-work inputs. No universal absence of aggregation/interface effects or direct new folding/structure determination is inferred.

records.description: Crystallize pKSI Y16S/D40N with one equivalent equilenin by hanging-drop mixing of 2 microlitres 30 mg/ml protein stock and 2 microlitres reservoir containing 0.9 M ammonium sulfate and 40 mM potassium phosphate pH 7.2. Grow at 20 C, cryoprotect using sodium malonate and collect 100 K diffraction. Molecular replacement, refinement and a held-out 5% diffraction subset yield deposited model 3IPT.
records.name: Prepared pKSI Y16S/D40N equilenin crystal
openObligations: The new crystal is the double mutant Y16S/D40N with an intermediate analogue, not the catalytically assayed Y16S single mutant with reacting 5(10)-EST. D40N is introduced to mimic the protonated general-base state ; transferring structural interpretation to catalysis is conditional.

Crystal data are collected at 100 K after crystallization at 20 C. The crystallization reservoir is pH 7.2 in SI, rounded to pH 7 in main text; neither equals a measured catalytic trajectory at room temperature.

Distances are refined model quantities. The 6.4 angstrom Ser16-to-equilenin oxygen separation excludes that direct donor geometry in this crystal, but does not directly observe a transition state, proton transfer, electric field or hydrogen-bond energy.

Table S3 gives 1.63 angstrom limiting resolution, 82.3% completeness, Rwork 20.7% and Rfree 24.5%. Four monomers in one asymmetric unit and their approximately 0.1 angstrom distance spread are not four independent crystals or a universal coordinate error.

Diffuse triangular density near the ligand is consistent with partially disordered water. SI says two-water split-occupancy modeling was imperfect and the cavity density was left empty in the final model. records.name: Conditional KSI mutation and solvation interpretation
openObligations: The new crystal is the double mutant Y16S/D40N with an intermediate analogue, not the catalytically assayed Y16S single mutant with reacting 5(10)-EST. D40N is introduced to mimic the protonated general-base state ; transferring structural interpretation to catalysis is conditional.

Crystal data are collected at 100 K after crystallization at 20 C. The crystallization reservoir is pH 7.2 in SI, rounded to pH 7 in main text; neither equals a measured catalytic trajectory at room temperature.

Distances are refined model quantities. The 6.4 angstrom Ser16-to-equilenin oxygen separation excludes that direct donor geometry in this crystal, but does not directly observe a transition state, proton transfer, electric field or hydrogen-bond energy.

The smaller 190-260-fold losses of Y16A/G/S/T versus the 19,000-fold Y16F loss do not isolate a single hydrogen bond. Mutations alter solvation, packing and potentially other energetic contributions; the source emphasizes that comparisons must specify the water-solvated reference reaction.

A water-filled cavity and a more desolvating Phe surface are source-supported mechanistic interpretations, not direct observations of the transient reacting dienolate or an experimental decomposition of transition-state stabilization.

The proposed approximately 200-fold Tyr16 contribution relative to aqueous hydrogen bonding is explicitly crude and assumes cavity-water energetics resemble the solution reference and no propagating structural effects. It is not an admitted exact universal catalytic energy.
No new constant electric field, universal active-site mechanism, cofactor requirement, global conformational coupling, regulatory pathway or proto-life function follows.

limitations: The observable is the 248 nm time-dependent absorbance converted using product molar absorptivity 14,800 M^-1 cm^-1. kcat and KM are fitted initial-rate parameters; KM is not automatically a substrate equilibrium dissociation constant and kcat/KM is not kcat.

The SI specifies enzyme concentration varied over at least a fourfold range and at least three assays, but does not print absolute kinetic enzyme concentrations. Do not import the millimolar NMR concentrations or 30 mg/ml crystallization stock as kinetic concentrations.

The reported errors are standard deviations across at least three assays, not full parameter covariance, a confidence interval or proof of independent laboratory reproduction. Values are reported as printed; neither fitted time courses nor uncertainty propagation were replayed.

For 5(10)-EST, the source invokes chemistry-limited turnover based on previous studies; that kinetic assignment was not independently tested here. Earlier 5-AND results have a different rate-limiting-step boundary and cannot be substituted as the same effect size.

The Y16F Table S2 row prints kcat=5.4x10^-4 s^-1, KM=41 micromolar, kcat/KM=8(1) M^-1 s^-1 and ratio 70,000. The central kcat and KM give about 13.2 M^-1 s^-1 rather than 8. Preserve this unresolved printed-table conflict; do not silently repair a cell, recalculate a new fit or claim internal exact agreement.

The experiment compares declared protein variants. No enzyme-free aqueous reaction rate, universal enzyme-versus-water acceleration, in-vivo metabolic flux, allosteric regulation or all-enzyme rate law is measured.
